# aidial_interceptor (Resource)

Manages an interceptor in DIAL Core (`PUT /v1/interceptors/{bucket}/{path}`). Models reference interceptors by name in their `interceptors` list.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "aidial_interceptor" "example" {
  bucket       = "platform"
  path         = "my-interceptor"
  display_name = "Content filter"
  description  = "Checks chat completions before they reach the model"
  endpoint     = "https://interceptor.example.invalid/intercept"

  forward_auth_token = true
  max_retry_attempts = 2

  default_headers = {
    "X-Team" = "platform"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bucket` (String) Target DIAL bucket. Must be "platform".
- `endpoint` (String) URL DIAL Core calls to run the interceptor.
- `path` (String) Interceptor path inside the bucket. DIAL Core accepts letters, digits and `._%:@[]()-`, so it cannot contain `/`.

### Optional

- `catalog_properties` (Dynamic) Catalog metadata of the interceptor (free-form object, sent as `catalogProperties`).
- `catalog_schema_id` (String) URI (`$id`) of the catalog schema describing `catalog_properties`, for example the `schema_id` of an `aidial_catalog_schema`.
- `default_headers` (Map of String) Additional headers sent with every request to the interceptor's endpoint.
- `defaults` (Dynamic) Default request parameters (free-form object, sent to DIAL as-is).
- `description` (String) Interceptor description.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable interceptor name.
- `display_version` (String) Version shown for the interceptor.
- `features` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--features))
- `forward_auth_token` (Boolean) Forward the caller's authorization token to the interceptor. DIAL Core defaults to false.
- `icon_url` (String) URL of the interceptor icon.
- `interfaces` (Attributes Map) Per-interface deployment configuration, keyed by DIAL Core interface type: `openaiChatCompletions`, `openaiEmbeddings`, `openaiResponses`, `anthropicMessages`. The keys are Core's camelCase names and are sent as written; the attributes inside each entry use snake_case. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces))
- `max_retry_attempts` (Number) Maximum number of retry attempts. DIAL Core defaults to 1.
- `name` (String) Interceptor name sent in the DIAL API request body. DIAL Core derives the name from the bucket and path, so it can be omitted; then it is read back from the API.
- `user_roles` (Set of String) Roles allowed to use the interceptor.

### Read-Only

- `api_name` (String) Canonical interceptor name returned by the DIAL API.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier in the form <bucket>/<path>.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = aidial_interceptor.example
  id = "platform/my-interceptor"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <bucket>/<path>. DIAL Core accepts only the "platform" bucket for interceptors.
terraform import aidial_interceptor.example platform/my-interceptor
```
